title: bug: create_epic, update_epic, delete_epic and delete_task record no actor on EPIC_CREATED / EPIC_UPDATED / EPIC_DELETED / TASK_DELETED (update_epic even deletes the proxy-injected workerId), so get_activity_log by workerId misses every epic edit and every task delete (last members of the c05bf92d / 2e3012b9 actor family)
description:
Filed by governor-e6b40560 from item (a) of defect hunt #7 (task-44785c82, architect-1dd28c7c, #governors msg-2dd55925). The hunt held it back until task-68a47060 landed, because both touch StateManager createEpic. 68a47060 is now DONE (9d08bab8).

PROBLEM (verified by reading moe/work-2026-10-24 at cc84c88a)
- tools/createEpic.ts, tools/deleteEpic.ts and tools/deleteTask.ts never read params.workerId. They call state.createEpic(input), state.deleteEpic(epicId) and state.deleteTask(taskId), and none of those takes an actor.
- tools/updateEpic.ts:52 runs `delete raw.workerId` (its comment says "update_epic doesn't use it") before strict-field validation, then calls state.updateEpic(epicId, updates).
- StateManager.ts createEpic (:1244), updateEpic (:1285) and deleteEpic (:1310) append EPIC_CREATED, EPIC_UPDATED and EPIC_DELETED without actorWorkerId, the last parameter of appendActivity (:552). deleteTask (:674) does the same for TASK_DELETED.
- Every sibling already records the caller:
  - create_task (c05bf92d): StateManager.createTask(input, actorWorkerId)
  - report_blocked, request_replan, archive_task and submit_plan_critique (2e3012b9)
  - the review loop (d981e0b0)
  - add_comment, amend_plan_step and release_task (e977c32b)
  - archive_epic (1064df99 / b9119a93)

EFFECT
get_activity_log { workerId } omits every epic a seat creates, edits or deletes, and every task delete. A per-seat audit cannot see who deleted a row or rewrote an epic.

REPRO
/mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-44785c82/A/epicDeleteActor.test.ts, a vitest file meant for packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/. Seat 'architect-c' makes a create_task baseline call, then create_epic, update_epic, delete_epic and delete_task. get_activity_log { workerId: 'architect-c' } should return [EPIC_CREATED, EPIC_DELETED, EPIC_UPDATED, TASK_CREATED, TASK_DELETED]. It returns only TASK_CREATED.

FIX SHAPE (the architect decides)
- Thread an optional actorWorkerId through StateManager createEpic, updateEpic, deleteEpic and deleteTask into appendActivity, the way createTask does.
- Pass params.workerId from all four tools.
- update_epic keeps workerId out of the epic's stored fields and out of its strict-field check, but uses it as the actor.
- Everything else about the events, payloads included, stays as it is.

Gate: narrow, per the standing epic-be924fb8 ruling (msg-bbf4f109). Run the four tools' test files plus the ported repro.
definitionOfDone: create_epic, update_epic, delete_epic and delete_task record the caller's workerId as the actor on EPIC_CREATED, EPIC_UPDATED, EPIC_DELETED and TASK_DELETED, so get_activity_log { workerId } returns all four; a call without workerId still succeeds and records no actor.
update_epic still refuses unknown fields and never stores workerId on the epic, but no longer discards it as the actor.

A daemon regression test (the hunt repro ported into packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/) fails before the fix and passes after it, and the existing createEpic, updateEpic, deleteEpic and deleteTask test files still pass.

implementationPlan.description:
State layer: thread an optional trailing `actorWorkerId?: string` into appendActivity's 7th argument (state/activityLog.ts:37 and :83). It is the same channel taskStore.createTask has used since c05bf92d.
- StateManager.createEpic(input, actorWorkerId?): the EPIC_CREATED appendActivity (~:1279) gains `, actorWorkerId`. Add the c05bf92d comment: the actor is a parameter, never read from `input`, because WebSocketServer's CREATE_EPIC passes its raw /ws payload as `input`.
- StateManager.updateEpic(epicId, updates, actorWorkerId?): EPIC_UPDATED (~:1300) gains `, actorWorkerId`.
- StateManager.deleteEpic(epicId, actorWorkerId?): the cascade loop calls `this.deleteTask(task.id, actorWorkerId)`, and EPIC_DELETED becomes `appendActivity('EPIC_DELETED' as ActivityEventType, { title: epic.title }, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, actorWorkerId)`. Keep the epic slot undefined so the event keeps its current shape: no top-level epicId, payload { title }.
- The StateManager.deleteTask delegator (~:674) and taskStore.deleteTask(state, taskId, actorWorkerId?) (~:690) pass the actor to TASK_DELETED (~:743). Change both signatures in lockstep, as the 'signatures generated from the extracted functions' comment requires.
Leave every other caller actor-less and byte-identical:
- the board's /ws DELETE_TASK, CREATE_EPIC, UPDATE_EPIC and DELETE_EPIC (WebSocketServer.ts:651-688; a human, with no seat id);
- archive_epic's updateEpic to status ARCHIVED (archiveEpic.ts:92);
- the rail-proposal updateEpic (StateManager.ts:1434).
Never substitute a placeholder ('unknown', 'agent', the assignee) for a missing actor. An explicit '' passes through, as on the sibling sites. Error handling: the existing error handling is unchanged. The audit append stays best-effort (appendActivity never throws into the caller), and every existing refusal keeps its order: Project not loaded, Epic not found, Task not found, the closeOpenAttempts failure that aborts a delete before any change, and non-ENOENT unlink errors. Edit with the session's own editing tool (Edit on a Claude seat, apply_patch on a codex exec seat), never a shell write. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-3e1d0c2e/reference-fix.diff is the runtime change the gate went green on (+29/-24 over 6 files). Use it as a reference only.
implementationPlan.note: Optional trailing actorWorkerId on StateManager createEpic/updateEpic/deleteEpic (cascade passes it to deleteTask)/deleteTask delegator and taskStore.deleteTask, into appendActivity's 7th arg. EPIC_DELETED keeps the epic slot undefined (no top-level epicId). WebSocketServer, archiveEpic.ts:92 and the rail-proposal updateEpic untouched; no test spies on these methods' arg lists.

implementationPlan.description:
Tools: pass the caller to the state layer. Each inputSchema gains `workerId: { type: 'string', description: 'Caller worker ID (auto-injected by proxy); recorded as the actor of <EVENT>' }`, an additive change like archiveEpic.ts:41 and createTask.ts:42. Each params type gains `workerId?: string`.
- create_epic: `state.createEpic({...}, params.workerId)`.
- delete_epic: `state.deleteEpic(params.epicId, params.workerId)`. Its tasksInEpic count and the cascadeDelete refusal stay as they are.
- delete_task: `state.deleteTask(params.taskId, params.workerId)`.
- update_epic: replace `const raw = ...; delete raw.workerId;` and its 'update_epic doesn't use it' comment with `const { workerId, ...raw } = (args || {}) as Record<string, unknown>;`, plus a comment that workerId is the EPIC_UPDATED actor, never an epic field. Do NOT add workerId to allowedFields; the set and the strict loop stay unchanged. Any other unknown field is then still refused with INVALID_INPUT before any write, and workerId never reaches `updates` (validateEpicUpdates would refuse it there). Pass `workerId as string | undefined` as updateEpic's third argument. The caller's args object is no longer mutated.
Pass the bare params.workerId everywhere, never a fallback. Error handling: missingRequired, notFound, notAllowed and invalidInput keep their order and messages, and a refused call writes nothing and records no event. (a3) and the existing updateEpic.test.ts case 'rejects unknown epic update fields' pin this. Edit with the session's own editing tool, never a shell write.
implementationPlan.note: Each of the four tools gains an optional workerId schema property and passes bare params.workerId to the state layer. update_epic now splits workerId off via destructuring (args no longer mutated); allowedFields and the strict loop unchanged.

Added workerId?: string to the Parameters blocks of moe.create_epic, moe.update_epic, moe.delete_task (now a two-field block) and moe.delete_epic, with the trailing commas. Nothing else in those sections touched.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
appendActivity(event, payload, task, worker, proposal, epic, actorWorkerId) is the only actor channel. An event's top-level workerId is worker?.id || proposal?.workerId || actorWorkerId, and get_activity_log { workerId } filters on that field alone. EPIC_DELETED is appended without the epic entity, so it has no top-level epicId; tests find it by event type. McpAdapter passes args raw, with no schema validation, so delete_task and delete_epic already receive the proxy's workerId and ignore it.
